fields.Frequency: Initial: once per entity; Renewal: annual for 5 entities
fields.Participants: Legal & Compliance Officer, CFO, VP Legal, Procurement Specialist

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-logof "Legal & Compliance Officer manages PHILGEPS registration for" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "verify PCAB license currency" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document management per DOC-001" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Registration lapse**: Expired PHILGEPS registration disqualifies BuildRight from all government bidding; automated renewal alerts critical
System Touchpoints: - PHILGEPS registration tracking in compliance module (W1950.3)
- Document storage for registration certificates (W1950.3)
- Integration with W22.1 (regulatory permits) for consolidated compliance view

steps.activity: Legal & Compliance Officer manages PHILGEPS registration for each entity: (a) BuildRight Depot, Inc. (primary — retail operations), (b) BuildRight Logistics, Inc. (if supplying logistics services to government), (c) register at philgeps.gov.ph with: SEC registration, mayor's permit, BIR registration, audited financial statements, PCAB license (if applicable for construction supply), (d) obtain "Red" or "Platinum" membership (Platinum required to download bidding documents and submit bids; web-verified — PhilGEPS tiers are Red/Platinum only)

Annual renewal: (a) update financial statements, (b) renew mayor's permit and business registration, (c) update contact information and authorized representatives, (d) verify PCAB license currency, (e) submit renewal 30 days before expiration

System integration: (a) PHILGEPS registration status tracked per entity in vendor master, (b) renewal calendar alerts 60 days before expiration, (c) registration certificate stored in document management per DOC-001

fields.Participants: Trade Account Manager, Credit Analyst, Sales Team, VP Store Operations
fields.Trigger: Government agency or LGU first purchase request

workflows.name: Government Entity Account Creation & Credit Assessment

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Account Manager creates government account" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-request of "request as billing basis" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "verify per entity" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-379 (ensure controlled execution — Government Registration & Qualification (PA-46.1).)
- operational: Trade Account Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Payment delays**: Government entities may pay beyond terms due to bureaucratic processes; factor longer collection cycle into cash flow planning
System Touchpoints: - Government customer master with entity classification (W1951.3)
- EWT configuration for government sales (W1951.3)
- Integration with W24 (credit application) for account setup process

steps.activity: Trade Account Manager creates government account: (a) entity type classification: national government agency, GOCC, LGU, state university, government hospital, public school, (b) collect: official designation, head of procuring entity (HOPE) name, procurement officer contact, billing address, TIN, (c) government accounts exempt from standard credit scoring — credit worthiness based on government entity status and approved budget

Credit Analyst sets government account terms: (a) credit limit: based on entity's annual procurement budget (if disclosed) or historical purchase pattern, (b) payment terms: government accounts typically Net 30–60 per government procurement law, (c) mandatory: government purchase order or purchase request as billing basis, (d) BIR withholding tax handling: government entities withhold 1% EWT per revenue regulation

System setup: (a) government account flag in customer master, (b) VAT treatment: government purchases are VAT-inclusive (BuildRight charges 12% VAT; government entity may be VAT-exempt per specific law — verify per entity), (c) EWT handling: system configured for 1% EWT on government sales, (d) payment terms and credit limit configured

fields.Participants: Trade Account Manager, VP Store Operations, Regional Manager, Category Manager

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Account Manager develops government account relationships" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews key government accounts" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "catalogs and pricing guides to government procurement offices" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-379 (ensure controlled execution — Government Registration & Qualification (PA-46.1).)
- operational: Trade Account Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Political sensitivity**: Government relationship management requires strict adherence to anti-bribery laws per GOV-013; document all interactions and gifts/hospitality
System Touchpoints: - Government account CRM tracking with engagement history (W1952.1)
- Annual procurement plan opportunity tracking (W1952.1b)
- Integration with W156 (CDP) for government account 360 view

steps.activity: Trade Account Manager develops government account relationships: (a) identify key decision-makers: procuring entity head, BAC (Bids and Awards Committee) members, end-user department heads, (b) understand entity's annual procurement plan (APP) — when do they plan to purchase building materials?, (c) position BuildRight as preferred supplier: product range, nationwide coverage (200 stores), delivery capability, BIR compliance

Quarterly: Trade Account Manager reviews key government accounts: (a) purchase history and trends, (b) upcoming procurement opportunities from APP, (c) competitive landscape: which other suppliers serve this entity?, (d) plan engagement activities: site visits, product presentations, facility tours

Annual: participate in LGU development planning: (a) attend pre-procurement conferences, (b) provide product catalogs and pricing guides to government procurement offices, (c) register for LGU supplier databases beyond PHILGEPS (some LGUs maintain separate registries)

fields.Participants: Trade Account Manager, Category Manager, VP Store Operations
fields.Trigger: Daily PHILGEPS and government procurement portal monitoring
fields.Volume: ~50–100 government procurement notices reviewed/week; ~5–10 opportunities pursued

workflows.name: Government Procurement Calendar Monitoring & Opportunity Identification

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "monitors procurement opportunities" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews opportunity pipeline" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-notify of "notify Category Manager for pricing preparation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-379 (ensure controlled execution — Government Registration & Qualification (PA-46.1).)
- operational: Trade Account Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Volume of notices**: Thousands of procurement notices posted daily; automated filtering by category keywords and geography essential
System Touchpoints: - PHILGEPS integration for automated opportunity alerts (W1953.1)
- Government procurement pipeline tracking (W1953.2)
- Integration with W130 (competitive intelligence) for market pricing

steps.activity: Daily: Trade Account Manager monitors procurement opportunities: (a) PHILGEPS portal for new bidding opportunities in hardware/building materials categories, (b) LGU procurement portals for local government opportunities, (c) PhilGEPS shopping/small-value procurement modes (same portal as (a); 'G-EPS' is its legacy name), (d) DPWH, DepEd, DOH, DND procurement notices for infrastructure, school, hospital, and military construction projects

Weekly: Trade Account Manager reviews opportunity pipeline: (a) filter by: (i) product relevance (does BuildRight carry the requested items?), (ii) geographic coverage (can BuildRight deliver to project sites?), (iii) value threshold (pursue opportunities > PHP 500K), (iv) competitiveness (does BuildRight have pricing advantage?), (b) categorize: hot (bidding deadline within 2 weeks), warm (bidding in 2–8 weeks), cold (advance notice only)
For hot opportunities: (a) notify Category Manager for pricing preparation, (b) coordinate with VP Store Operations for bid/no-bid decision, (c) begin bid preparation per W1959

fields.Participants: Tax Accountant, Legal & Compliance Officer, CFO
fields.Trigger: Annual tax clearance; government bidding requirement

workflows.name: BIR Tax Clearance & Government Supplier Compliance Maintenance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Accountant obtains BIR tax clearance per entity" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document package" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "tracks compliance document expiration" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-379 (ensure controlled execution — Government Registration & Qualification (PA-46.1).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Bid disqualification**: Expired or missing compliance documents result in automatic bid disqualification; automated monitoring essential
System Touchpoints: - Compliance document repository with expiration tracking (W1954.3)
- Integration with W90 (monthly tax filing) for tax clearance support
Time Estimate: - 2–3 days/entity/year for tax clearance; 1–2 days/bid for document compilation

steps.activity: Annual: Tax Accountant obtains BIR tax clearance per entity: (a) BIR Form 0605 (Registration Update), (b) certification of no pending tax cases, (c) proof of timely filing of monthly/quarterly returns, (d) tax clearance valid for 1 year — maintain current clearance for all 5 entities

Per bid: compile compliance document package: (a) BIR tax clearance, (b) SEC registration, (c) mayor's permit / business permit, (d) PHILGEPS registration certificate, (e) audited financial statements (latest), (f) PCAB license (if required for construction supply), (g) BIR registration certificate, (h) mother company certification (if bidding on behalf of subsidiary)

System tracks compliance document expiration: (a) automated alerts 30 days before expiration, (b) document repository for quick retrieval during bid preparation, (c) compliance status dashboard per entity

fields.Participants: VP Store Operations, Trade Account Manager, Legal & Compliance Officer
fields.Trigger: Annual training cycle; new staff onboarding

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document preparation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "recorded in HR system per W51" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-379 (ensure controlled execution — Government Registration & Qualification (PA-46.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Staff turnover**: Loss of trained government sales staff to competitors; cross-train multiple team members to prevent single-point-of-failure
System Touchpoints: - Training tracking in HR module (W1955.3)
- Integration with W51 (training management) for certification

steps.activity: Annual training on RA 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act): (a) modes of procurement: competitive bidding, shopping, negotiated procurement, small value procurement, (b) bidding process: eligibility, technical, financial components, (c) BuildRight's obligations as winning bidder: delivery timeline, warranty, quality standards, (d) prohibited acts: bribery, collusion, bid rigging per GOV-013, (e) sanctions for non-compliance: blacklisting, suspension from government procurement

Practical training: (a) PHILGEPS portal navigation, (b) bid document preparation: eligibility requirements, technical proposal, financial proposal, (c) government billing and collection procedures, (d) EWT handling for government sales, (e) mock bidding exercise

Staff certification: (a) training completion recorded in HR system per W51, (b) government procurement certification linked to role competency, (c) only certified staff authorized to prepare and submit government bids

fields.Participants: Trade Account Manager, Credit Analyst, Sales Associate
fields.Volume: ~50–100 active institutional accounts (schools, hospitals, churches, NGOs)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Account Manager qualifies institutional account" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "Credit assessment for institutional accounts" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-create of "create institutional account in customer master" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-379 (ensure controlled execution — Government Registration & Qualification (PA-46.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Credit risk**: Institutional accounts (especially NGOs and smaller schools) may have higher default risk than government accounts; stricter credit limits recommended; mitigated by CTL-379 (controlled execution — Government Registration & Qualification (PA-46.1))
System Touchpoints: - Institutional customer master with entity type classification (W1956.3)
- Integration with W24 (credit application) for credit assessment
- Integration with W460 (trade account onboarding) for onboarding process

steps.activity: Trade Account Manager qualifies institutional account: (a) entity type: private school, private hospital, church/religious organization, NGO, foundation, cooperative, (b) collect: SEC/DSWD registration, TIN, authorized representative, billing address, (c) assess purchase potential: annual building material spend estimate

Credit assessment for institutional accounts: (a) unlike government accounts, institutional accounts require standard credit scoring per W24, (b) credit check: financial statements, trade references, bank references, (c) credit limit and terms set per standard trade account policy: Net 30 for established institutions, COD for new/risky accounts

Onboarding: (a) create institutional account in customer master, (b) assign pricing tier: institutional pricing (typically 5–10% below SRP for bulk purchases), (c) provide account credentials for BuildRight institutional ordering (if available), (d) assign dedicated Sales Associate or Trade Account Manager

fields.Participants: VP Store Operations, Trade Account Manager, CFO, VP Merchandising

workflows.name: Government Supplier Performance Scorecard & Annual Review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Account Manager compiles annual government sales scorecard" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review to executive team" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-collect of "CFO reviews government sales profitability" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-379 (ensure controlled execution — Government Registration & Qualification (PA-46.1).)
- operational: VP Store Operations review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin pressure**: Government competitive bidding drives prices down; ensure minimum margin thresholds are maintained in bid pricing
System Touchpoints: - Government sales analytics dashboard (W1957.1)
- Integration with W35 (management reporting) for consolidated view

steps.activity: Trade Account Manager compiles annual government sales scorecard: (a) total government revenue by entity type (national govt, LGU, GOCC, institutional), (b) number of bids submitted, won, and lost with win rate, (c) average deal size, (d) collection performance: DSO for government accounts vs. trade accounts, (e) top 10 government accounts by revenue, (f) government sales as % of total revenue (target: 3–5%)

VP Store Operations presents government sales review to executive team: (a) performance vs. prior year, (b) pipeline for next year (known upcoming government projects), (c) competitive landscape: which competitors are winning government bids?, (d) strategic recommendations: expand/contract government sales focus

CFO reviews government sales profitability: (a) gross margin on government sales vs. retail/trade, (b) collection cost: government accounts may require more collection effort, (c) working capital impact: longer payment terms tie up cash, (d) EWT recovery: ensure 1% EWT is properly credited against income tax
